extracted.intended_audience: Peer reviewers for PLOS ONE (scientists and researchers asked to review manuscripts)
extracted.subtask_description: Completing the PLOS ONE reviewer form to evaluate a scientific manuscript against the journal's publication criteria, including technical soundness, statistics, data availability, and clarity of presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the manuscript technically sound, and do the data support the conclusions?
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript must describe a technically sound piece of scientific research with data that supports the conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiments must have been conducted rigorously, with appropriate controls, replication, and sample sizes. The conclusions must be drawn appropriately based on the data presented. (This is a required response on the form.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Has the statistical analysis been performed appropriately and rigorously?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of whether statistical methods and their application are appropriate for the data and questions addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select whether the statistical analysis has been performed appropriately and rigorously. (No further text on the form; reviewers are expected to judge appropriateness, assumptions, tests, and interpretation.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Have the authors made all data underlying the findings in their manuscript fully available?
rubrics_metrics.description: The PLOS Data policy requires authors to make all data underlying the findings fully available without restriction, with rare exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data should be provided as part of the manuscript or supporting information, or deposited to a public repository. In addition to summary statistics, the data points behind means, medians, and variance measures should be available. If there are restrictions on publicly sharing data (e.g. participant privacy or third-party data), those must be specified in the Data Availability Statement in the manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the manuscript presented in an intelligible fashion and written in standard English?
rubrics_metrics.description: Language must be clear, correct, and unambiguous because PLOS ONE does not copyedit accepted manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should note any typographical or grammatical errors to be corrected at revision and should specify particular errors. (This is a required response on the form.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Review Comments to the Author (explain answers and raise concerns)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the main body of the review explaining answers to the above questions and any additional comments for the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this space to explain your assessments of technical soundness, statistics, data availability, and presentation. You may also include concerns about dual publication, research ethics, or publication ethics. If the review exceeds 20,000 characters, upload it as an attachment. (The form enforces a 200–20,000 character limit for this field.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Consent for publication of peer review and reviewer identity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the reviewer consents to have their identity published if the authors choose to publish the peer review history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you choose 'no', your identity will remain anonymous but your review may still be made public. If you choose 'yes', provide your full name as it should appear in the published peer review. See the Privacy Policy for information about consent withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential to Editor — Competing interests disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare any potential or perceived competing interests that may influence the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consult the Competing Interests policy and declare any potential interests the Editor should be aware of; if none, write 'I have no competing interests.' This information is visible only to the editor and journal office. (Limit 20,000 characters.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential to Editor — Assistance in preparing the review
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether anyone (e.g., post-doc or graduate student) assisted in preparing the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If assistance was received, provide the assistant's name and title here. If you have revealed your identity to the authors, include the assistant's name in the public name field as well. (Optional; limit 200 characters.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential to Editor — Should the submission be highlighted if accepted?
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional recommendation on whether the accepted submission should be highlighted on the PLOS ONE website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is optional. Note that PLOS ONE does not evaluate manuscripts based on perceived significance or readership; this question is for editorial/promotional consideration only.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID reviewer credit / authorization note
rubrics_metrics.description: Information about depositing the review to ORCID and the default authorization status for ORCID reviewer credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: the reviewer's default response may be 'No' so the Review will not be sent to ORCID; proxy reviewers cannot change this at submission — the actual reviewer must log in to their account and authorize ORCID deposit later if desired. (Procedural guidance rather than evaluation criterion.)
